title: 29 U.S.C. § 1132 — ERISA Civil Enforcement (§ 502)
built_by: Claude (assistant) under direction of Michael Hartmann

evolution_stages.key_change: New disclosure obligations added; § 1132(c)(1) penalty scope expanded; core (a)(1)(B)/(a)(2)/(a)(3) unchanged

case_law.rule: § 1132(a)(3) authorizes traditional equitable remedies including surcharge, reformation, estoppel, and disgorgement; individual make-whole relief available

case_law.case: Firestone Tire & Rubber Co. v. Bruch
case_law.rule: Standard of review under § 1132(a)(1)(B): abuse of discretion if plan grants discretionary authority; de novo if not; conflict of interest is a factor

primary_claims: § 1132(a)(1)(B): recovery of frozen pension benefits due as active participant
§ 1132(a)(2) + § 1109: fiduciary breach in processing unauthorized retirement election
§ 1132(a)(3) + Amara: equitable restoration of accrual status; disgorgement of fraudulent payments
§ 1132(c)(1): written demand for plan documents within 30 days; $110/day penalty begins immediately on failure
primary_application.first_action: Send written request for Summary Plan Description and plan document to UA Local 342 pension plan administrator. Trigger § 1132(c)(1) 30-day clock.

outstanding_work: Primary-source opinion text capture (opinion.txt) for both cases
Request and review UA Local 342 plan document (Summary Plan Description) to determine discretionary authority grant
Verify whether unauthorized election constitutes a 'denial' triggering exhaustion or an unauthorized transaction excusing exhaustion
Document DOL-OIG criminal referral pathway (§ 1028 identity theft + § 664 ERISA theft from employee benefit plan)
